subject: Food Science
title: Fiber and Gut Health
description: A quick win: understand Fiber and Gut Health.

hook.text: You can't digest fiber. But the trillions of bacteria in your gut can—and they reward you for feeding them.

buildup.text: Soluble fiber dissolves in water and forms a gel. Insoluble fiber stays intact and adds bulk to digestion.

discovery.text: Gut bacteria ferment soluble fiber into short-chain fatty acids, which feed colon cells and reduce inflammation.

twist.text: Most people eat only 15g of fiber daily—half the recommended 25–30g. Chronic diseases correlate with the shortfall.

climax.text: High-fiber diets are linked to lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, and colon cancer across dozens of studies.

punchline.text: Feed your bacteria and they protect you. Fiber is the deal.

quiz.question: What do gut bacteria produce when they ferment soluble fiber?
options: Short-chain fatty acids that feed colon cells
